text:
# Toyota_Human_Handover_Agent: the only place where a call is passed to a contact centre person
# (journey 01, "Every Call": Start Of The Call; Handing Over And Callbacks).
# Reached four ways:
#   1. from the supervisor with one entry marker (a typed value that says why the caller was routed
#      here): entry_person, entry_complaint, entry_chase, entry_stop_calling or entry_identity_failed.
#      The marker narrows the triage to the two or three needs it can mean, and is consumed.
#      A marker is acted on only when exactly one of the five is true: two or more at once are
#      values that reached this agent without being passed for this entry and say nothing, so
#      they are all put back and the entry is read as if no marker had come. A summary, a queue
#      and a booking reference that arrive together with a marker are kept;
#   2. from any specialist that could not finish (its one-way escape), with handover_reason and
#      handover_summary set, and handover_queue and booking_reference when it has them;
#   3. from the outbound agent with a summary and no handover_reason (a call it made, or a call to
#      the number it calls out from): the request is worked out from the conversation and the
#      summary is kept. It may pass a marker as well: its summary, queue and booking reference
#      then stay with the call;
#   4. from an agent's ON_ERROR, with nothing at all: when the conversation shows no request that
#      belongs here, it is system trouble and the caller goes to a person (reason system_error).
# Leaf agent: it hands off to nobody. A live transfer is an ESCALATE to the contact centre queue.
#   E27  asks for a person: the queue is checked, then the call is passed to a person with a summary
#   E28  upset or complaining: acknowledged first, then passed to a person with a summary
#   Q03  OPEN  the summary that travels with the call; what else the contact centre needs is not agreed
#   E29  nobody in the contact centre is free: a queue callback is offered instead
#   Q01  OPEN  callbacks are booked 9 am to 6 pm, later only when the customer asks; a caller who
#        asks to be called back gets the callback, not a transfer
#   A03  asked for a manager: a manager callback, never a transfer to another contact centre agent
#   N21  OPEN  complaint: details taken, ticket raised, ticket number by SMS, complaints team calls back
#   A02  a chase is recognised straight away: open requests are looked up on the caller's number
#   Q04  OPEN  chase rule: follow-up email on the second call, complaint on the third
#   N23  OPEN  returned missed call: says why we called (a lead, a reminder or a callback) and asks;
#        the supervisor routes the caller's answer to the specialist who picks it up
#   N25  OPEN  "stop calling me": do not call is recorded and confirmed; data questions go to a person
# Demo overlay (journey 09, owned by the ai_summit_demo profile; the gates are steps here):
#   E122 the caller asked for a person or a manager: the close line, and end_call is returned
#   E123 any other road to a person: the advisor line, then the closing question, and the
#        demonstration carries on
#   E120 no attendee is asked for a name or a number: a complaint is not taken at the Summit, it
#        takes the road to a person and so gets the advisor line (assumption, not in the document)
# end_call reaches the supervisor only when the supervisor itself routed the caller here. After
# a specialist's one-way escape the close line is still said, but nothing this agent sets can
# end the session: that needs a change outside this file (reported).
# Environment flags read here (unset means the interim behaviour of the use-case document):
#   TOYOTA_DEMO_MODE                           "true": no live transfer (E122, E123)
#   TOYOTA_HANDOVER_COMPLAINT_MODE             "transfer": complaints go to a person instead of a ticket (N21)
#   TOYOTA_HANDOVER_CHASE_SECOND_CALL          "person": the second chase call goes to a person (Q04)
#   TOYOTA_HANDOVER_MISSED_CALL_RETURN         "false": a returned missed call is not looked up (N23)
#   TOYOTA_HANDOVER_DNC_RECORD                 "false": a stop-calling request goes to a person (N25)
#   TOYOTA_HANDOVER_CALLBACK_LATER_ON_REQUEST  "false": no callback later than the window, even on request (Q01)
# handover_reason: specialists send any short snake_case code. Five kinds are acted on:
# caller_upset and complaint make the acknowledgement of E28 come before the connecting line;
# a code that starts with manager (manager_requested) becomes a manager callback, never a
# transfer (A03); callback_requested becomes a callback, not a transfer (Q01);
# roadside_transfer_failed is urgent (the roadside queue, no callback offer); and
# caller_asked, callback_requested or a manager code is what "asked for a person" means in
# the demo (E122).
# For callers who come from the supervisor this agent writes the code itself, with the same
# words the specialists use (caller_asked, caller_upset) plus manager_requested, data_question,
# complaint, system_error and the like.
# Queues: the queue that is checked is the queue the call is sent to. It is toyota_service
# unless the escape says toyota_sales or the matter is a sales one, complaints for a complaint
# that goes to a person, roadside for an urgent matter, and the general queue
# toyota_contact_centre for a name that is none of these.
# Returned to the supervisor: end_call (true only after the demo close line).
# Also kept for the rest of the call, in this agent: caller_name when a name was taken for a
# complaint, and contact_mobile once a caller accepted or gave a number for a callback or a
# ticket message. The supervisor does not map these two back yet (reported), so today only a
# later visit to this agent benefits.
AGENT: Toyota_Human_Handover_Agent
VERSION: "0.2.0"
DESCRIPTION: "Passes the call to a contact centre person with a summary, and handles callbacks, complaints, chases of earlier requests, returned missed calls and do-not-call requests"

GOAL: |
  When a caller needs a person, get them one without making them repeat anything: pass the
  call to a contact centre person together with a summary, or, when nobody is free, arrange a
  callback and say exactly when it will come. Arrange a manager callback when a manager is
  asked for. Take a complaint and raise it, follow up an earlier request the caller is
  chasing, say why we called when a caller returns a missed call, and record a request to
  stop calling. Every outcome ends with one short sentence saying what happens next and when.
  A caller who stays on the line is then asked once, by a fixed step, whether they need
  anything else.

PERSONA: |
  You are the Toyota voice assistant for Al-Futtaim in the UAE, at the moment a caller needs a
  person, a callback or a complaint taken. Calm, brief and clear. You take ownership,
  acknowledge once how the caller feels, and never argue or blame anyone.

LIMITATIONS:
  - "Only store what each step asks for. The steps after you check the queue, connect the call, arrange callbacks, raise complaints and record requests. Never transfer, end or escalate the call yourself and never promise a transfer before the queue has been checked."
  - "Asked for a manager: a manager calls back. Never transfer a manager request to another contact centre agent."
  - "Never agree a discount or a price, never promise the outcome of a complaint, a refund or compensation, and never say who was at fault."
  - "When explaining why we called, give only the general reason. Never read out names, plate numbers, dates, amounts or other record details before the caller has been confirmed."
  - "Never answer questions about the caller's personal data or how we got their number, and never give legal advice. Those go to a person."
  - "Never collect or promise an email. Never name agents, systems, tools, queues or settings to the caller."
  - "Do not greet, do not replay a welcome, do not say goodbye and do not ask whether there is anything else: a fixed step asks that once when the task is done."
  - "Never say that you are checking or looking something up, and never speak a hold line: one is played for you while a system answers. When a step tells you to end your turn with no text, write nothing at all."
  - "If the caller asks for something else, such as a booking, a price or a question about a car, do not decline and do not try to do it: hand the message back with __return_to_parent__ when you have that tool. Without it, say one of our team will help with that too and carry on."
  - "Safety first: if the caller mentions a warning light, a leak, smoke, a noise, a brake or steering problem, a breakdown, an accident, someone hurt or locked in the car, or says they are afraid to drive, hand the message back at once with __return_to_parent__ when you have that tool. Without it: when the car is not safe to drive, the caller is unsure or afraid, or it is a breakdown, an accident, an injury or someone locked in, store request_type = safety_emergency and set request_changed to true, so the caller is connected to the roadside team's queue at once. For anything milder, carry on so a person hears it, and put the concern first in the hand-over summary when the step shows you that summary."
  - "A mobile number the caller has just given is read back in full, in groups of three or four digits, and used only after a yes. A number we already hold is never read out: say only its last three digits."

LANGUAGE: "en"

INSTRUCTIONS: |
  1. A caller who asks for a person is passed to a contact centre person with a summary. The
    queue is checked first. When nobody is free, a callback from the contact centre is offered.
    A caller who asks to be called back gets the callback, not a transfer.
  2. A caller who is upset is acknowledged once, then passed to a person in the same way.
  3. A caller who asks for a manager gets a manager callback, never a transfer.
  4. A caller who wants to raise a complaint: take what happened, when and where, raise it,
    send the ticket number by text message and say when the complaints team will call.
  5. A caller who is chasing an earlier request: find it on their number and record the chase.
    The contact centre rule decides what is done; say what it did.
  6. A caller who returns a missed call: say the general reason we called and ask how you
    can help. The right specialist picks up their answer.
  7. A caller who says stop calling me: record it and confirm it. Questions about their data
    go to a person.
  Values per current policy are never taken from here. The callback window (interim, open:
  later than the window only if the customer asks) and the time the complaints team calls
  are given by the step, from the tool or from the configured policy wording; the time the
  scheduling tool returns is the one to say.

# max_flow_iterations is the documented platform default, stated because this flow is made of
# many small fixed steps and one guide quotes a default of 100.
EXECUTION:
  temperature: 0.1
  max_reasoning_iterations: 4
  max_flow_iterations: 1500
  tool_timeout: 8000

USE BEHAVIOR_PROFILE: toyota_voice
USE BEHAVIOR_PROFILE: ai_summit_demo

# No CONVERSATION section: the toyota_voice profile owns tone, the two-sentence limit, the
# language policy, barge-in and the silence ladder for every agent.
# The project's hold lines, played by the runtime while a tool or a hand-over takes long. No
# flow step and no reasoning step speaks a hold line of its own.
MESSAGES:
  filler_general: "One moment please."
  filler_general_ar: "لحظة من فضلكم."
  filler_tool_call: "One moment please."
  filler_tool_call_ar: "لحظة من فضلكم."
  filler_handoff: "One moment please."
  filler_handoff_ar: "لحظة من فضلكم."

MEMORY:
  session:
    # Passed in by the supervisor or by the agent that escapes here (CONTEXT.pass).
    - NAME: caller_phone
      TYPE: string
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: customer_name
      TYPE: string
      DESCRIPTION: "Name on the profile. From the silent look-up alone it is not confirmed: it is used as the contact name only when identity_status is matched or confirmed"
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: caller_name
      TYPE: string
      DESCRIPTION: "The caller's own name as they gave it. Store it here when a step asks you to take their name"
    - NAME: crm_customer_id
      TYPE: string
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: identity_status
      TYPE: string
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: contact_mobile
      TYPE: string
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: plate_number
      TYPE: string
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: vehicle_model
      TYPE: string
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: booking_reference
      TYPE: string
      DESCRIPTION: "The booking the request is about, when the agent that escaped here knew one"
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: handover_reason
      TYPE: string
      DESCRIPTION: "Short code for why a person is needed. Set by the specialist that handed over, or by this flow just before the transfer"
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: handover_summary
      TYPE: string
      DESCRIPTION: "Two or three plain English sentences for the person who takes over: who is calling, what they wanted, what was done on this call, what is still needed"
    - NAME: handover_queue
      TYPE: string
      DESCRIPTION: "Queue named by the agent that escaped here: toyota_service or toyota_sales. Read once at entry; the flow works with route_queue"
      READONLY: true
    # Entry markers (CONTRACT): one is passed as true to say why the supervisor routed the
    # caller here. Each is consumed (set to false) in the step that acts on it. A marker is
    # acted on only when it is the one marker that is true; with two or more true they are all
    # put back unused (drop_markers). They start as false, so "not true" is a plain comparison.
    - NAME: entry_person
      TYPE: boolean
      INITIAL: false
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: entry_complaint
      TYPE: boolean
      INITIAL: false
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: entry_chase
      TYPE: boolean
      INITIAL: false
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: entry_stop_calling
      TYPE: boolean
      INITIAL: false
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: entry_identity_failed
      TYPE: boolean
      INITIAL: false
      READONLY: true
    # Returned to the supervisor: true only after the demo close line (E122).
    - NAME: end_call
      TYPE: boolean
      INITIAL: false
      READONLY: true
    # Working values of this agent.
    - NAME: entry_summary
      TYPE: string
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: entry_reason
      TYPE: string
      DESCRIPTION: "The handover_reason this visit started with, empty when the supervisor passed the caller in. A different reason later means a specialist has handed the caller over while this agent was waiting"
      INITIAL: ""
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: triage_hint
      TYPE: string
      DESCRIPTION: "Set by the flow from the entry marker: which needs the caller can have. Empty when no marker came with the call"
      INITIAL: ""
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: reentry_count
      TYPE: number
      INITIAL: 0
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: request_type
      TYPE: string
      DESCRIPTION: "What the caller needs: caller_asked (a person now), callback_requested (a call back from a person), manager_requested, caller_upset, complaint, chase, missed_call, stop_calling, data_question, other_request, safety_emergency or withdrawn. Stays pending until it is clear"
      INITIAL: "pending"
    - NAME: request_changed
      TYPE: boolean
      DESCRIPTION: "True when, part-way through a step, the caller asks for a different one of the needs listed in request_type"
      INITIAL: false
    - NAME: wants_data_answer
      TYPE: boolean
      DESCRIPTION: "True when a caller who asked us to stop calling also asks how we got their number or about their data"
      INITIAL: false
    - NAME: sales_matter
      TYPE: boolean
      DESCRIPTION: "True when what the caller needs is about buying a car, a sales enquiry or a test drive"
      INITIAL: false
    - NAME: caller_statement
      TYPE: string
      DESCRIPTION: "One plain English sentence saying what the caller wants"
    - NAME: person_reason
      TYPE: string
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: route_queue
      TYPE: string
      DESCRIPTION: "Contact centre queue that is checked and that the call is sent to: toyota_service, toyota_sales, complaints, roadside or toyota_contact_centre. Only the flow writes it"
      INITIAL: "toyota_service"
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: urgent_transfer
      TYPE: boolean
      INITIAL: false
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: contact_name
      TYPE: string
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: reference_note
      TYPE: string
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: reach_number
      TYPE: string
      DESCRIPTION: "Mobile number used for callbacks, messages, look-ups and do not call, in international format: a plus sign, the country code, then the digits, for example +971501234567"
    - NAME: reach_last_digits
      TYPE: string
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: local_date
      TYPE: string
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: local_weekday
      TYPE: string
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: local_time
      TYPE: string
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: queue_open
      TYPE: boolean
      SOURCE: tool
    - NAME: can_hold
      TYPE: boolean
      DESCRIPTION: "True when the queue was checked on this visit and is open with everyone on another call, so the caller may hold for the next free person"
      INITIAL: false
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: callback_type
      TYPE: string
      INITIAL: "queue_callback"
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: callback_decision
      TYPE: string
      DESCRIPTION: "The caller's answer to the callback offer: accepted, declined or wait. Stays pending until they answer"
      INITIAL: "pending"
    - NAME: callback_preferred_time
      TYPE: string
      DESCRIPTION: "Callback time the caller asked for, as a date and time in UAE time with the +04:00 offset, for example 2026-10-08T16:30:00+04:00. Leave unset when they gave none"
    - NAME: callback_later_requested
      TYPE: boolean
      DESCRIPTION: "True only when the caller asked for a callback later than the normal callback window"
      INITIAL: false
    - NAME: callback_language
      TYPE: string
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: callback_summary
      TYPE: string
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: callback_scheduled_for
      TYPE: string
      SOURCE: tool
    - NAME: complaint_details
      TYPE: string
      DESCRIPTION: "The complaint in the caller's own words, in plain English, with the date and the service centre or showroom involved"
    - NAME: complaint_category
      TYPE: string
      DESCRIPTION: "One of service_quality, repeat_problem, billing, delay, staff_conduct, sales, delivery, unanswered_request, other"
      INITIAL: "other"
    - NAME: complaint_ready
      TYPE: boolean
      DESCRIPTION: "True when the complaint details are taken and the number for the ticket message is confirmed"
      INITIAL: false
    - NAME: complaint_created
      TYPE: boolean
      SOURCE: tool
    - NAME: complaint_ticket_number
      TYPE: string
      SOURCE: tool
    - NAME: complaint_response_time
      TYPE: string
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: ticket_message_sent
      TYPE: boolean
      INITIAL: false
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: open_requests_list
      TYPE: array
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: chase_request_id
      TYPE: string
      DESCRIPTION: "Id of the open request the caller is chasing, copied exactly from the list, or none when no listed request fits. Stays pending until it is clear"
      INITIAL: "pending"
    - NAME: chase_note
      TYPE: string
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: chase_action_taken
      TYPE: string
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: chase_ticket_number
      TYPE: string
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: chase_expected_response
      TYPE: string
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: missed_call_reason
      TYPE: string
      READONLY: true
    # The sentence a reasoning step worded for the caller, in the caller's language. A fixed
    # step (say_spoken_line) says it, so that the closing question always comes after it: when
    # a reasoning step speaks and the flow goes on in the same turn, the platform puts the next
    # fixed line first.
    - NAME: spoken_line
      TYPE: string
      DESCRIPTION: "One or two short sentences for the caller, worded exactly as they are to be said on the phone. Write it only when a step asks for it"
      INITIAL: ""
    # True once the live hand-over to a person was started on this visit (connect_person). A
    # failure after that is the hand-over itself: it is not tried a second time.
    - NAME: transfer_started
      TYPE: boolean
      INITIAL: false
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: failure_count
      TYPE: number
      INITIAL: 0
      READONLY: true
    - NAME: reroute_count
      TYPE: number
      INITIAL: 0
      READONLY: true

TOOLS:
  get_queue_status(queue: string) -> {open: boolean, agents_available: number, estimated_wait_seconds: number}
    description: "Check whether the contact centre queue is open and whether an agent is free right now. Use before handing a call to a person so a queue callback can be offered when nobody is free."
    auth_profile: "toyota_contact_centre_api"
    effect: read_only
    confirm: never
    params:
      queue:
        description: "Queue name: toyota_contact_centre (the general queue, used when no other fits), toyota_service, toyota_sales, complaints or roadside"
    on_result:
      set:
        queue_open: result.open
        queue_agents_available: result.agents_available

  schedule_callback(callback_type: string, mobile_number: string, reason: string, summary: string, preferred_time?: string, language?: string, customer_name?: string) -> {scheduled: boolean, callback_id: string, scheduled_for: string}
    description: "Arrange a call back to the customer. Callback type is one of queue_callback (nobody free), manager_callback (asked for a manager), bad_line. A sales callback travels on the lead, and a Hindi or Urdu callback is a send_team_request. The backend enforces the callback window, per current policy. Returns the time the customer will be called (scheduled_for, ISO 8601 with +04:00) so it can be read back."
    auth_profile: "toyota_contact_centre_api"
    effect: side_effect
    side_effects: true
    confirm: never
    params:
      callback_type:
        description: "Kind of callback, from the list in the description"
      mobile_number:
        description: "Number to call back, E.164"
      reason:
        description: "Why the callback is needed, in a few words"
      summary:
        description: "What happened on this call so the person calling back does not ask again"
      preferred_time:
        description: "Time the customer asked for, ISO 8601 with +04:00, when given"
      language:
        description: "Language to call back in: en or ar"
      customer_name:
        description: "Customer's name, when known"
    on_result:
      set:
        callback_scheduled: result.scheduled
        callback_scheduled_for: result.scheduled_for

  create_complaint(mobile_number: string, category: string, details: string, customer_name?: string, plate_number?: string, centre_id?: string) -> {created: boolean, ticket_number: string, response_time: string}
    description: "Raise a complaint ticket with the complaints team, as the contact centre does today. Returns the ticket number and, in words, when the complaints team will call (response_time). The complaints system sends no SMS for a ticket the AI agent raises: send the ticket number with send_customer_message, template complaint_ticket. A repeat problem or a bill higher than quoted goes to the service advisor with send_team_request unless the caller asks to complain."
    auth_profile: "toyota_contact_centre_api"
    effect: side_effect
    side_effects: true
    confirm: never
    params:
      mobile_number:
        description: "Customer's mobile number, E.164"
      category:
        description: "One of service_quality, repeat_problem, billing, delay, staff_conduct, sales, delivery, unanswered_request, other, per current policy"
      details:
        description: "The complaint in the customer's words, with dates and the centre or showroom involved"
      customer_name:
        description: "Customer's name, when known"
      plate_number:
        description: "Plate of the car concerned"
      centre_id:
        description: "Service centre or showroom concerned: a centre_id from find_service_centres or a showroom_id from find_showrooms, when known"
    on_result:
      set:
        complaint_created: result.created
        complaint_ticket_number: result.ticket_number

  get_open_requests(mobile_number?: string, customer_id?: string, reference?: string) -> {total: number, requests: {request_id: string, type: string, team: string, created_date: string, chase_count: number, status: string, summary: string}[], last_outbound_call_reason: string, last_outbound_call: {reason_code: string, record_reference: string, called_at: string, team: string}}
    description: "Find what is already open for this caller: earlier team requests, callbacks, complaints, and why we last called them. Give at least one of mobile_number, customer_id or reference. Use when the caller is chasing a team, following up, or returning a missed call from our number. type is one of team_request, callback, complaint. team is a team from send_team_request, or a queue from get_queue_status for a callback. status is open or in_progress, per current policy. last_outbound_call says why we last called: reason_code is one of lead, booking_reminder, callback, survey, other, and record_reference is the lead, booking or callback it was about; its fields are empty when we did not call. last_outbound_call_reason is the same reason in words."
    auth_profile: "toyota_contact_centre_api"
    effect: read_only
    confirm: never
    params:
      mobile_number:
        description: "Caller's mobile number, E.164"
      customer_id:
        description: "Customer profile identifier from lookup_customer_by_phone or search_customer, for a caller on another number"
      reference:
        description: "Request identifier or complaint ticket number the caller reads from the SMS"
    on_result:
      set:
        open_request_count: result.total
    MODEL_CONTEXT:
      FIELDS: [total, requests[].request_id, requests[].type, requests[].team, requests[].chase_count, requests[].status, requests[].summary, last_outbound_call_reason, last_outbound_call.reason_code, last_outbound_call.record_reference, last_outbound_call.called_at, last_outbound_call.team]

  record_chase(request_id: string, summary: string) -> {chase_count: number, action_taken: string, action_code: string, ticket_number: string, expected_response: string}
    description: "Record that the customer chased an open request again. The contact centre rule decides the action from the chase count, per current policy. action_code is one of none, followup_email, complaint; action_taken says the same in words so it can be said on the call. When a complaint is raised, ticket_number is its ticket and expected_response says in words when the complaints team will call."
    auth_profile: "toyota_contact_centre_api"
    effect: side_effect
    side_effects: true
    confirm: never
    params:
      request_id:
        description: "Open request identifier from get_open_requests"
      summary:
        description: "What the customer said on this call"

  record_do_not_call(mobile_number: string, requested_by: string) -> {recorded: boolean}
    description: "Record that the customer asked us to stop calling, then confirm it to them."
    auth_profile: "toyota_contact_centre_api"
    effect: side_effect
    side_effects: true
    confirm: never
    params:
      mobile_number:
        description: "Number to stop calling, E.164"
      requested_by:
        description: "Who asked: always customer_on_call"
    on_result:
      set:
        do_not_call_recorded: result.recorded

  send_customer_message(mobile_number: string, template: string, channel?: string, reference?: string, reference_type?: string, language?: string) -> {sent: boolean, channel_used: string, message_id: string}
    description: "Send one templated message to the customer by SMS or WhatsApp. Templates: service_booking_confirmation (link to add to calendar, reschedule, cancel or track), service_booking_cancellation (confirms that the booking is cancelled), service_tracking_link (link to follow a car in the workshop), body_shop_tracking_link (link to the body shop tracking portal), test_drive_details (day, time, showroom map link, what to bring, confirmed or waiting for the showroom), location_and_hours, complaint_ticket, survey_invite. This is the only sender: the booking, sales and complaints systems send no message for records the AI agent creates. Always confirm the last digits of the number first. Can be sent again when the caller says it did not arrive. channel_used is sms or whatsapp."
    auth_profile: "toyota_notify_api"
    effect: side_effect
    side_effects: true
    confirm: never
    params:
      mobile_number:
        description: "Mobile number that receives the message, E.164"
      template:
        description: "Template name from the list in the description"
      channel:
        description: "sms or whatsapp. Leave empty to use the default configured in the notify service. The service does not fall back by itself: when a whatsapp send returns sent false, send once more with sms"
      reference:
        description: "Identifier the template is filled from: a booking reference, a test-drive reference, a complaint ticket number, a centre_id or a showroom_id"
      reference_type:
        description: "What the reference is: one of service_centre, showroom, booking, complaint. Needed for location_and_hours, which takes a service centre or a showroom"
      language:
        description: "en or ar, matching the language of the call"
    on_result:
      set:
        message_sent: result.sent

  get_local_date_time() -> {date: string, weekday: string, time: string, iso_datetime: string}
    description: "Get today's date, weekday and time in the UAE. Call it before working out a day from words such as today, tomorrow, Thursday or next Thursday, so that the date comes from a fact. date is YYYY-MM-DD, time is HH:MM, iso_datetime is ISO 8601 with +04:00, and weekday is one of monday, tuesday, wednesday, thursday, friday, saturday, sunday."
    auth_profile: "toyota_booking_api"
    effect: read_only
    confirm: never

CONSTRAINTS:
  # Hard gates on the tools that change something. The flow already routes this way; the
  # constraints make sure no other path can reach these tools. A failed gate goes to a person.
  always:
    # N25: do not call is recorded only when the caller asked for it
    - REQUIRE request_type == "stop_calling" BEFORE calling record_do_not_call
      ON_FAIL:
        GOTO: tool_failed
    # E29, A03: a callback is arranged only after the caller accepted it
    - REQUIRE callback_decision == "accepted" BEFORE calling schedule_callback
      ON_FAIL:
        GOTO: tool_failed
    # N21: a complaint is raised only when the details are taken and the number is confirmed
    - REQUIRE complaint_ready == true BEFORE calling create_complaint
      ON_FAIL:
        GOTO: tool_failed
    # N21: the only message this agent sends is the ticket number of a complaint it has just
    # raised with create_complaint, by SMS (the complaints system sends none for such a ticket)
    - REQUIRE complaint_created == true BEFORE calling send_customer_message
      ON_FAIL:
        GOTO: tool_failed
    # A02, Q04: a chase is recorded only against a request the caller identified
    - REQUIRE chase_request_id != "pending" AND chase_request_id != "none" BEFORE calling record_chase
      ON_FAIL:
        GOTO: tool_failed

# How the flow is built: reasoning steps only talk to the caller and store values; every tool
# call, every branch (CHECK with ON_FAIL, or ON_RESULT) and every counter is a deterministic step.
# Reasoning steps are given one harmless read-only tool in AVAILABLE_TOOLS (the UAE clock, which
# takes no input and writes nothing) so that the tools that change something, and the queue
# check whose result the flow branches on, are never on the model's menu (an empty list is not
# documented to mean "none").
# A reasoning step that only stores values ends its turn with no text: the step after it
# speaks, or a tool runs and the runtime plays the hold line.
# Order of speech: when a reasoning step speaks and the flow goes on in the same turn, the
# platform says the next fixed line first and the step's own words after it. So no reasoning
# step speaks an outcome that a fixed line follows. The three outcome sentences (callback
# arranged, complaint raised, chase recorded) are written to spoken_line by the model and said
# by the fixed step say_spoken_line; the closing question then comes last. A step that stores a
# decision says nothing with it.
# New entry while a step is waiting: this agent keeps its place when it hands a request back, so
# a later entry can find it inside a step. Every step that talks to the caller therefore also
# ends when a new entry is seen, which is a reason code that differs from the one this visit
# started with, or an entry marker that is true (markers are consumed at the start of a visit,
# so a true one is always new). The gate after the step then takes the entry from the top.
FLOW:
  entry_point: start

  steps:
    - start
    - name_gate
    - use_profile_name
    - entry_person_gate
    - enter_person
    - person_demo_gate
    - entry_complaint_gate
    - enter_complaint
    - entry_chase_gate
    - enter_chase
    - entry_stop_gate
    - enter_stop_calling
    - entry_identity_gate
    - enter_identity_failed
    - drop_markers
    - reason_gate
    - escape_entry
    - urgent_roadside
    - escape_upset_gate
    - acknowledge_upset
    - understand_request
    - after_understand
    - request_unclear
    - route_stop_calling
    - route_lookup
    - route_complaint
    - route_upset
    - route_safety
    - route_withdrawn
    - request_dropped
    - route_other
    - route_pending
    - other_gate
    - system_trouble_entry
    - reentry_gate
    - takeover_start
    - restart_routing
    - person_gate
    - demo_gate
    - demo_close
    - demo_out_of_scope
    - summary_gate
    - build_summary
    - manager_gate
    - urgent_gate
    - callback_request_gate
    - sales_gate
    - queue_sales
    - queue_gate
    - queue_general
    - check_queue
    - connect_person
    - callback_clock
    - callback_offer_gate
    - offer_queue_callback
    - manager_callback_start
    - offer_manager_callback
    - after_callback_offer
    - callback_decision_gate
    - callback_wait_gate
    - callback_declined
    - callback_number_gate
    - callback_later_gate
    - callback_window_only
    - schedule_callback_step
    - confirm_callback
    - say_outcome_gate
    - say_spoken_line
    - say_outcome_done
    - callback_failed
    - callback_not_arranged
    - complaint_mode_gate
    - complaint_demo_gate
    - complaint_transfer_ack
    - take_complaint
    - after_complaint
    - complaint_ready_gate
    - raise_complaint
    - send_ticket_message
    - confirm_complaint
    - complaint_to_person
    - complaint_failed
    - dnc_mode_gate
    - missed_call_mode_gate
    - number_gate
    - number_missing_gate
    - contact_task_gate
    - record_dnc
    - confirm_dnc
    - dnc_followup_gate
    - dnc_to_person
    - data_to_person
    - number_missing
    - lookup_requests
    - choose_request
    - after_choose_request
    - chase_match_gate
    - record_chase_step
    - tell_chase_outcome
    - chase_to_person
    - second_chase_to_person
    - missed_call_lead
    - missed_call_reminder
    - missed_call_callback
    - explain_missed_call
    - ask_how_to_help
    - tool_failed
    - count_failure
    - transfer_not_made
    - tool_trouble_line
    - hard_failure
    - hard_failure_route
    - ask_anything_else
    - finish

  # Entry. The working values are set afresh on every visit. What came with the call is then
  # read in this order: an entry marker from the supervisor, a reason code from a specialist's
  # escape, or neither (the triage then works from the conversation).
  # The queue named by the escape is copied once into route_queue (toyota_service when absent).
  # Q03: the booking reference that came with the escape is turned into a note for the summary
  # that goes with a callback; it is empty when there is no reference.
  # Only a real phone number in international format counts (a withheld caller id is not one).
  # end_call is put back to false on every visit: it is true only after the demo close line of
  # this visit, never left over from an earlier one whose close could not end the session.
  start:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      end_call = false
      spoken_line = ""
      transfer_started = false
      request_type = "pending"
      request_changed = false
      wants_data_answer = false
      sales_matter = false
      caller_statement = ""
      person_reason = ""
      triage_hint = ""
      urgent_transfer = false
      can_hold = false
      entry_summary = FIRST_NON_EMPTY(handover_summary, "")
      entry_reason = COALESCE(handover_reason, "")
      route_queue = FIRST_NON_EMPTY(handover_queue, "toyota_service")
      contact_name = COALESCE(FIRST_NON_EMPTY(caller_name, ""), "")
      reference_note = REGEX_REPLACE(COALESCE(booking_reference, ""), "^(.+)$", "Booking reference: $1.")
      callback_type = "queue_callback"
      callback_decision = "pending"
      callback_later_requested = false
      complaint_details = ""
      complaint_category = "other"
      complaint_ready = false
      complaint_response_time = ""
      ticket_message_sent = false
      chase_request_id = "pending"
      chase_action_taken = ""
      chase_ticket_number = ""
      chase_expected_response = ""
      missed_call_reason = ""
      local_date = ""
      local_weekday = ""
      local_time = ""
      failure_count = 0
      reroute_count = 0
      reach_number = COALESCE(FIRST_NON_EMPTY(REGEX_EXTRACT(contact_mobile, "^[+][0-9]{8,15}$"), REGEX_EXTRACT(caller_phone, "^[+][0-9]{8,15}$")), "")
      reach_last_digits = COALESCE(REGEX_EXTRACT(FIRST_NON_EMPTY(REGEX_EXTRACT(contact_mobile, "^[+][0-9]{8,15}$"), REGEX_EXTRACT(caller_phone, "^[+][0-9]{8,15}$")), "[0-9]{3}$"), "")
    THEN: name_gate

  # The contact name for a callback or a complaint. The caller's own name comes first. The
  # name on the profile is used only once the caller has been identified: from the silent
  # look-up alone it is not confirmed.
  name_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: contact_name == "" AND (identity_status == "matched" OR identity_status == "confirmed")
    ON_FAIL: entry_person_gate
    THEN: use_profile_name

  use_profile_name:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      contact_name = COALESCE(FIRST_NON_EMPTY(customer_name, ""), "")
    THEN: entry_person_gate

  # ---- Why the call came here: entry markers from the supervisor ----------------------------
  # One marker says, as a typed value, why the supervisor routed the caller here. The step that
  # acts on a marker consumes it, so a later entry for another reason never finds a stale one.
  # A marker is acted on only when it is the one marker that is true (CONTRACT section 1). Each
  # gate below therefore asks for its own marker and for the other four not to be true. Two or
  # more true at once are values that reached this agent without being passed for this entry:
  # none of the gates passes, drop_markers puts all five back, and the entry is read as it was
  # before markers existed (a reason code, or the triage on the conversation).
  # A marker entry carries no reason code: one left from an earlier visit is dropped. A summary,
  # a queue and a booking reference that arrive together with the marker are kept (start has
  # already read them into entry_summary, route_queue and reference_note): the outbound agent
  # can so pass a marker and keep all three. The marker narrows the triage to the needs it can
  # mean; with no marker and no reason code the triage runs as before.
  # E27, A03, Q01: the caller asked for a person, a manager, or a call back from a person.
  entry_person_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: entry_person == true AND entry_complaint != true AND entry_chase != true AND entry_stop_calling != true AND entry_identity_failed != true
    ON_FAIL: entry_complaint_gate
    THEN: enter_person

  enter_person:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      entry_person = false
      entry_reason = ""
      triage_hint = "The caller asked for a person or a manager. Store manager_requested if they asked for a manager or a supervisor, callback_requested if they asked to be called back rather than to speak to someone now, otherwise caller_asked."
    CLEAR: [handover_reason, handover_queue]
    THEN: person_demo_gate

  # E122 (demo overlay): asked for a person at the Summit. The close line follows at once, with
  # no model step in between.
  person_demo_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: ("{{env.TOYOTA_DEMO_MODE}}" == "true")
    ON_FAIL: understand_request
    THEN: demo_close

  # E28, N21: the caller is upset, or wants to raise or follow up a complaint.
  entry_complaint_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: entry_complaint == true AND entry_person != true AND entry_chase != true AND entry_stop_calling != true AND entry_identity_failed != true
    ON_FAIL: entry_chase_gate
    THEN: enter_complaint

  enter_complaint:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      entry_complaint = false
      entry_reason = ""
      triage_hint = "The caller is upset or has a complaint. Store complaint if they want to raise a complaint, chase if they are following up a complaint they have already raised, otherwise caller_upset."
    CLEAR: [handover_reason, handover_queue]
    THEN: understand_request

  # A02, Q04, N23: the caller is chasing an earlier request or returning a missed call.
  entry_chase_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: entry_chase == true AND entry_person != true AND entry_complaint != true AND entry_stop_calling != true AND entry_identity_failed != true
    ON_FAIL: entry_stop_gate
    THEN: enter_chase

  enter_chase:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      entry_chase = false
      entry_reason = ""
      triage_hint = "The caller is chasing an earlier request or returning a missed call. Store missed_call if they say that someone called them or that they are returning our call, otherwise chase."
    CLEAR: [handover_reason, handover_queue]
    THEN: understand_request

  # N25: stop calling me, or how did you get my number.
  entry_stop_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: entry_stop_calling == true AND entry_person != true AND entry_complaint != true AND entry_chase != true AND entry_identity_failed != true
    ON_FAIL: entry_identity_gate
    THEN: enter_stop_calling

  enter_stop_calling:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      entry_stop_calling = false
      entry_reason = ""
      triage_hint = "The caller wants us to stop calling them, or asks how we got their number. Store stop_calling if they want the calls to stop, and also set wants_data_answer to true if they ask about their data as well. Store data_question if they only ask how we got their number or what data we hold about them."
    CLEAR: [handover_reason, handover_queue]
    THEN: understand_request

  # Two identity passes left the caller unknown and they still need help with a service
  # request: no triage and no question, a person takes over (E27, with the summary of Q03).
  entry_identity_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: entry_identity_failed == true AND entry_person != true AND entry_complaint != true AND entry_chase != true AND entry_stop_calling != true
    ON_FAIL: drop_markers
    THEN: enter_identity_failed

  enter_identity_failed:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      entry_identity_failed = false
      entry_reason = ""
      person_reason = "caller_not_identified"
    CLEAR: [handover_reason, handover_queue]
    THEN: person_gate

  # No single marker: none is true (a specialist's escape, the outbound agent, an agent's
  # ON_ERROR), or two or more are true at once and so say nothing about this call. All five are
  # put back to false, so that none is acted on and no later step takes one for a new entry.
  # What came with the call (reason code, summary, queue, booking reference) is left as it is.
  drop_markers:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      entry_person = false
      entry_complaint = false
      entry_chase = false
      entry_stop_calling = false
      entry_identity_failed = false
    THEN: reason_gate

  # No marker. A hand-over from a specialist arrives with handover_reason set and skips the
  # triage. With no reason code either (the outbound agent, or an agent's ON_ERROR), the
  # triage works out the request from the conversation.
  reason_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CLEAR: [handover_queue]
    CHECK: handover_reason IS SET AND handover_reason != ""
    ON_FAIL: understand_request
    THEN: escape_entry

  # The roadside transfer failed (reason code from the safety agent). Urgent: the roadside
  # queue, connected at once, with no queue check and no callback offer.
  escape_entry:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: handover_reason == "roadside_transfer_failed"
    ON_FAIL: escape_upset_gate
    THEN: urgent_roadside

  # Also taken when the caller reports a safety emergency inside this agent and the message
  # cannot be handed back (route_safety).
  urgent_roadside:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      route_queue = "roadside"
      urgent_transfer = true
    THEN: person_gate

  # E28 on a hand-over from a specialist: the specialist marks an upset caller with the reason
  # caller_upset or complaint, and the acknowledgement comes before anything else.
  escape_upset_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: handover_reason == "caller_upset" OR handover_reason == "complaint"
    ON_FAIL: person_gate
    THEN: acknowledge_upset

  # E28: the acknowledgement is a fixed line in its own step, so it is always said and always
  # comes before the connecting line, whichever way the caller reached this agent.
  acknowledge_upset:
    REASONING: false
    RESPOND: "I'm sorry about the trouble you've had."
    MESSAGE_KEY: upset_acknowledgement
    THEN: person_gate

  # A02: the need, a chase included, is recognised from the caller's first words. With an
  # entry marker the choice is narrowed to the needs that marker can mean (triage_hint).
  # E28: an upset caller is only recognised here; the step acknowledge_upset says the apology.
  # Q03: the summary for the person is written here when the call is going to a person.
  # The note that came with the call is shown to the model because callers who are passed on
  # without a reason code (a call made by the outbound agent, or a call to the number it calls
  # out from) arrive with a summary and it must not be lost.
  # The step speaks only when it has to ask. Once the need is stored it ends with no text:
  # the next step acknowledges, answers or connects, or a tool runs behind the hold line.
  # With no marker a request that is none of the listed needs is never handed back (the call
  # may have come from an agent's ON_ERROR, and handing it back could send it round again):
  # it is stored as other_request and a person takes over.
  # Limit: the caller is asked at most twice; the third unclear answer goes to a person.
  understand_request:
    REASONING: true
    GOAL: |
      The caller has just been passed to you. In this step you only work out what they need.
      From what they have already said, decide which ONE of these it is and store it in
      request_type. Go by what they asked for most recently, not by a request that was
      already dealt with earlier in the call:
      - caller_asked: asks for a person, an agent, an advisor or to be transferred.
      - callback_requested: asks to be called back by one of our team, now or at a time they
        name, rather than to speak to someone straight away.
      - manager_requested: asks for a manager or a supervisor, to speak to or to be called by.
      - caller_upset: is upset, angry or complaining, but has not asked to raise a complaint.
      - complaint: wants to raise a complaint.
      - chase: is chasing a team, a promised call or an earlier request, says nobody called
        back, or is following up a complaint they already raised.
      - missed_call: is returning a missed call from our number.
      - stop_calling: wants us to stop calling them or to remove their number.
      - data_question: asks how we got their number or what data we hold about them.
      - other_request: none of the above. They asked for none of these, so the call reached
        you because the assistant could not go on with what they wanted.
      - withdrawn: they say they no longer need anything from you (never mind, forget it).
      If they want us to stop calling and also ask about their data, store stop_calling and
      set wants_data_answer to true.
      {{#if triage_hint}}Why the call was routed to you: {{triage_hint}} Choose only from the values named in that note. If what they want is clearly something else, such as a booking, a price or a question about a car, hand it back with __return_to_parent__ and a note of what it is about. If you do not have that tool, store other_request.{{/if}}
      {{#if entry_summary}}Note that came with the call, for you only, never read out: {{entry_summary}}{{/if}}
      Also store caller_statement: one plain English sentence saying what the caller wants.
      For caller_asked, callback_requested, manager_requested, caller_upset, data_question and
      other_request also store handover_summary (two or three plain English sentences for the person who takes
      over: who is calling if known, what they want, what has been done on this call, what is
      still needed; keep every fact from the note that came with the call), and set
      sales_matter to true when it is about buying a car, a sales enquiry or a test drive.
      {{#if contact_name}}Caller's name, for the summary only, never said to the caller: {{contact_name}}.{{/if}}
      When you have stored request_type, end your turn with no text at all: the next step
      speaks. Never apologise or comment on how the caller feels in this step, never say that
      you are checking, and never promise a transfer, a callback or an outcome.
      Only if you cannot tell which one it is: ask one short question in the caller's
      language and leave request_type as pending.
      A safety problem with the car (a warning light, a leak, smoke, a noise, brakes or
      steering, a breakdown, an accident, someone hurt or locked in, or fear of driving): hand
      it back at once with __return_to_parent__ and a note of what it is about. Without that
      tool, store safety_emergency when the car is not safe to drive, the caller is unsure or
      afraid, or it is a breakdown, an accident, an injury or someone locked in; for anything
      milder store other_request and start handover_summary with the concern.
    AVAILABLE_TOOLS: [get_local_date_time]
    EXIT_WHEN: request_type != "pending" OR (handover_reason IS SET AND handover_reason != "" AND handover_reason != entry_reason) OR entry_person == true OR entry_complaint == true OR entry_chase == true OR entry_stop_calling == true OR entry_identity_failed == true
    MAX_TURNS: 3
    MAX_ATTEMPTS: 3
    ON_EXHAUSTED: request_unclear
    VOICE:
      END_OF_SPEECH_TURN_TYPE: open_ended_question
    THEN: after_understand

  # A new entry arrived while this agent was waiting in the step (see the note above FLOW):
  # take it from the top, with what came with it.
  after_understand:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: ((handover_reason IS SET AND handover_reason != "" AND handover_reason != entry_reason) OR entry_person == true OR entry_complaint == true OR entry_chase == true OR entry_stop_calling == true OR entry_identity_failed == true) AND reentry_count < 2
    ON_FAIL: route_stop_calling
    THEN: takeover_start

  request_unclear:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      person_reason = "not_understood"
    THEN: person_gate

  # Routing on request_type. Anything that is not a stop-calling request, a chase, a missed call,
  # a complaint or a dropped request goes to a person (caller_asked, manager_requested,
  # caller_upset, data_question, other_request, safety_emergency).
  route_stop_calling:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: request_type == "stop_calling"
    ON_FAIL: route_lookup
    THEN: dnc_mode_gate

  route_lookup:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: request_type == "chase" OR request_type == "missed_call"
    ON_FAIL: route_complaint
    THEN: missed_call_mode_gate

  route_complaint:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: request_type == "complaint"
    ON_FAIL: route_upset
    THEN: complaint_mode_gate

  # E28: an upset caller is acknowledged first, then passed to a person.
  route_upset:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: request_type == "caller_upset"
    ON_FAIL: route_safety
    THEN: acknowledge_upset

  # Safety inside this leaf agent. It declares no hand-off to the safety agent (that would
  # close a cycle). With the return tool the model hands a safety remark back and the
  # supervisor routes it. Without it (the caller came through a specialist's one-way escape)
  # an emergency takes the urgent road: the roadside queue at once, no callback offer. A milder
  # concern goes first in the summary and the caller carries on to a person.
  route_safety:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: request_type == "safety_emergency"
    ON_FAIL: route_withdrawn
    THEN: urgent_roadside

  # The caller has dropped the request (never mind). Nothing is arranged, raised or recorded
  # and nobody is called: a short acknowledgement, then the closing question.
  route_withdrawn:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: request_type == "withdrawn"
    ON_FAIL: route_other
    THEN: request_dropped

  request_dropped:
    REASONING: false
    RESPOND: "No problem."
    MESSAGE_KEY: no_problem
    THEN: ask_anything_else

  # A request that is none of this agent's own and could not be handed back.
  route_other:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: request_type == "other_request"
    ON_FAIL: route_pending
    THEN: other_gate

  # The need was never stored (the triage was left through a new entry that could no longer be
  # taken from the top): a person takes over, with the reason code not_understood.
  route_pending:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: request_type == "pending"
    ON_FAIL: person_gate
    THEN: request_unclear

  # With a note from the agent that passed the call (the outbound agent), a person simply takes
  # the request over. The same when a marker came with the call (the triage note is set): the
  # caller was routed here on purpose and wants something that could not be handed back. With
  # nothing at all, an agent's ON_ERROR passed the call here.
  other_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: (entry_summary IS SET AND entry_summary != "") OR (triage_hint IS SET AND triage_hint != "")
    ON_FAIL: system_trouble_entry
    THEN: person_gate

  # No marker, no reason code, no note, and nothing in the conversation that asks for a
  # person: system trouble. The caller hears that once, then takes the road to a person. It
  # counts as the first failure of the visit, so a failure after it is not announced again.
  system_trouble_entry:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      person_reason = "system_error"
      failure_count = 1
    RESPOND: "I'm sorry, I'm having trouble with that just now."
    MESSAGE_KEY: system_trouble
    THEN: person_gate

  # A step that talks to the caller ended because something changed. When a new entry has
  # arrived in the meantime (this agent keeps its place when it hands a request back, and the
  # caller may come back through the supervisor or through a specialist that needs a person),
  # the entry is taken from the top so that what came with it is used as it came. Otherwise
  # the caller changed their mind and the routing starts again.
  reentry_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: ((handover_reason IS SET AND handover_reason != "" AND handover_reason != entry_reason) OR entry_person == true OR entry_complaint == true OR entry_chase == true OR entry_stop_calling == true OR entry_identity_failed == true) AND reentry_count < 2
    ON_FAIL: restart_routing
    THEN: takeover_start

  # The entry is taken from the top. The counter keeps this road from being taken more
  # than twice in one visit, so it can never turn into a loop; after that the ordinary
  # restart applies, which ends with a person.
  takeover_start:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      reentry_count = ADD(reentry_count, 1)
    THEN: start

  # The caller changed their mind part-way through a step: start the routing again for the new
  # need. A third change of mind in one visit goes straight to a person, so this cannot loop.
  restart_routing:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      reroute_count = ADD(reroute_count, 1)
      request_changed = false
      person_reason = request_type
      callback_type = "queue_callback"
      callback_decision = "pending"
      callback_later_requested = false
      complaint_ready = false
      chase_request_id = "pending"
      can_hold = false
    CLEAR: [handover_summary, callback_preferred_time]
    CHECK: reroute_count < 3
    ON_FAIL: hard_failure
    THEN: route_stop_calling

  # ---- Passing the call to a person -------------------------------------------------------
  # Every road to a person passes this gate. The reason code is settled here: the one a step
  # set, else the one that came with the escape, else the need the triage stored.
  # Demo overlay (journey 09): no live transfer at the Summit.
  person_gate:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      person_reason = FIRST_NON_EMPTY(person_reason, handover_reason, request_type)
    CHECK: ("{{env.TOYOTA_DEMO_MODE}}" == "true")
    ON_FAIL: summary_gate
    THEN: demo_gate

  # E122: the caller asked for a person or a manager, to speak to or to be called by (the
  # supervisor's marker, the triage, or the reason code caller_asked or manager_requested from
  # a specialist): the close line.
  # E123: every other road to a person, such as a specialist's escape with any other reason:
  # the advisor line, and the demonstration carries on.
  demo_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: person_reason == "caller_asked" OR request_type == "caller_asked" OR person_reason == "callback_requested" OR request_type == "callback_requested" OR person_reason.matches("manager|supervisor") OR request_type.matches("manager|supervisor")
    ON_FAIL: demo_out_of_scope
    THEN: demo_close

  # E122: the demo close line. end_call goes back to the supervisor, which ends the session.
  demo_close:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      end_call = true
    RESPOND: "That's the end of this demonstration, and thank you for trying the Toyota voice assistant. For anything further, please speak to the team at the Toyota stand."
    MESSAGE_KEY: demo_close
    THEN: finish

  # E123: the advisor line. No end_call: the demonstration carries on. The line is a statement,
  # and the supervisor adds nothing after this agent returns, so the closing question follows
  # it: the attendee is not left in silence and knows that the next request is theirs to make.
  demo_out_of_scope:
    REASONING: false
    RESPOND: "For this, I'd normally connect you with an advisor."
    MESSAGE_KEY: demo_out_of_scope
    THEN: ask_anything_else

  # OPEN Q03 (contact centre): What else does the contact centre need to see?
  # Interim: the person gets the summary, the reason code, the queue, the caller's numbers and
  # names, whether the caller was identified, the car, the booking reference and the
  # conversation (ESCALATE.context_for_human). A summary that is already there is kept.
  summary_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: handover_summary IS SET AND handover_summary != ""
    ON_FAIL: build_summary
    THEN: manager_gate

  # Q03: the summary is written here when none came with the call. The step says nothing to
  # the caller: the connecting line, the callback offer or the hold line follows.
  build_summary:
    REASONING: true
    GOAL: |
      Write the hand-over summary for the contact centre person who takes this call and store
      it in handover_summary: two or three plain English sentences saying who is calling, what
      they wanted, what was done on this call and what is still needed. Use only what was said
      or done on this call.
      Why a person is needed: {{person_reason}}. If that says safety_emergency, start the
      summary with the safety problem in the caller's own words.
      {{#if caller_statement}}What the caller asked for: {{caller_statement}}{{/if}}
      {{#if entry_summary}}Summary written earlier on this call: {{entry_summary}}{{/if}}
      {{#if contact_name}}Caller's name: {{contact_name}}.{{/if}}
      {{#if vehicle_model}}Car: {{vehicle_model}}.{{/if}}
      {{#if plate_number}}Plate: {{plate_number}}.{{/if}}
      {{#if booking_reference}}Booking reference: {{booking_reference}}.{{/if}}
      {{#if complaint_details}}Complaint details taken: {{complaint_details}}{{/if}}
      {{#if chase_action_taken}}Chase recorded, result: {{chase_action_taken}}{{/if}}
      Also set sales_matter to true when the matter is about buying a car, a sales enquiry or
      a test drive.
      Ask the caller nothing and tell them nothing. When the summary is stored, end your turn
      with no text at all: the next step speaks.
    AVAILABLE_TOOLS: [get_local_date_time]
    EXIT_WHEN: always
    MAX_TURNS: 2
    THEN: manager_gate

  # A03: a manager request never reaches the transfer below. It becomes a manager callback.
  # The test is deliberately loose: any request type that names a manager or a supervisor, and
  # any reason code from a specialist that starts with manager (manager_requested and the like).
  manager_gate:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      handover_summary = FIRST_NON_EMPTY(handover_summary, entry_summary, caller_statement, "No summary was captured on this call. Please ask the caller how you can help.")
    CHECK: request_type.contains("manager") OR request_type.contains("supervisor") OR person_reason.matches("^manager")
    ON_FAIL: urgent_gate
    THEN: manager_callback_start

  # Urgent (the roadside transfer failed, or a safety emergency that could not be handed
  # back): connected at once to the roadside queue. No queue check and no callback offer.
  urgent_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: urgent_transfer == true
    ON_FAIL: callback_request_gate
    THEN: connect_person

  # Q01: the caller asked to be called back rather than to speak to someone now (the triage
  # stored it, or a specialist escaped with that reason code). The callback is arranged as
  # asked: there is no transfer, so no queue is checked.
  callback_request_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: request_type == "callback_requested" OR person_reason == "callback_requested"
    ON_FAIL: sales_gate
    THEN: callback_clock

  # The queue. route_queue is toyota_service unless the escape named another queue or a step
  # set one (complaints). A sales matter that is still on the service queue moves to the sales
  # queue. Only the flow writes the queue; the model only says whether it is a sales matter.
  sales_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: sales_matter == true AND route_queue == "toyota_service"
    ON_FAIL: queue_gate
    THEN: queue_sales

  queue_sales:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      route_queue = "toyota_sales"
    THEN: check_queue

  # A queue name that is not one of the contact centre's queues (a value an escaping agent
  # made up) falls back to the general queue, so the check and the transfer still agree.
  queue_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: route_queue == "toyota_service" OR route_queue == "toyota_sales" OR route_queue == "complaints" OR route_queue == "roadside" OR route_queue == "toyota_contact_centre"
    ON_FAIL: queue_general
    THEN: check_queue

  queue_general:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      route_queue = "toyota_contact_centre"
    THEN: check_queue

  # E29: before the hand-over, find out whether a contact centre person is free in the queue
  # the call will be sent to. When the status cannot be read, the transfer is tried anyway.
  # An open queue with nobody free is remembered (can_hold): the caller may then choose to hold.
  check_queue:
    REASONING: false
    CALL: get_queue_status
      WITH:
        queue: route_queue
      AS: queue_status
    ON_RESULT:
      - IF: queue_status.open == true AND queue_status.agents_available > 0
        THEN: connect_person
      - IF: queue_status.open == true
        SET:
          can_hold = true
        THEN: callback_clock
      - ELSE:
        THEN: callback_clock
    ON_FAILURE:
      THEN: connect_person

  # E27, E28, A03 (asked for a person: transfers), Q03: the call goes to the contact centre queue
  # with the summary. The caller hears what happens next, then the transfer starts.
  # transfer_started is raised here: if the transfer itself then fails, the failure lands on
  # tool_failed, which does not come back to this step (see "Failures").
  connect_person:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      handover_reason = FIRST_NON_EMPTY(person_reason, handover_reason, "caller_asked")
      transfer_started = true
    RESPOND: "I'll connect you with one of our team now. Please stay on the line."
    MESSAGE_KEY: connecting_to_person
    THEN: ESCALATE with REASON: "The caller needs one of our team"

  # ---- Callbacks --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Q01: a time the caller names ("tomorrow at four") is turned into a date from a fact, the
  # UAE date and time from the booking system's clock, not from the model's own idea of today.
  # When the clock cannot be read, no preferred time is sent and the time the caller asked for
  # goes into the summary in their own words. The branch asks for a real date (YYYY-MM-DD), so
  # it cannot match after a failed call.
  callback_clock:
    REASONING: false
    CALL: get_local_date_time
      AS: local_now
    ON_RESULT:
      - IF: local_now.date.matches("^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$")
        SET:
          local_date = local_now.date
          local_weekday = local_now.weekday
          local_time = local_now.time
        THEN: callback_offer_gate
      - ELSE:
        THEN: callback_offer_gate
    ON_FAILURE:
      THEN: callback_offer_gate

  callback_offer_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: callback_type == "manager_callback"
    ON_FAIL: offer_queue_callback
    THEN: offer_manager_callback

  # E29: nobody is free, so a queue callback is offered. The same step arranges a callback the
  # caller asked for (Q01).
  # OPEN Q01 (contact centre): Is this still right? Interim: callbacks 9 am to 6 pm, later only
  # if the customer asks. The window wording is the locale key policy_callback_window; the
  # backend enforces the window and the scheduling tool returns the time that is actually booked.
  # Limit: five turns without an answer, then the callback is treated as not arranged.
  offer_queue_callback:
    REASONING: true
    GOAL: |
      The caller needs one of our team. Why: {{person_reason}}.
      If that says callback_requested, they asked to be called back: say you can arrange
      that, and ask whether to call the number ending {{reach_last_digits}}.
      Otherwise nobody can take the call right now: say that in one short sentence and offer
      a callback from our team on the number ending {{reach_last_digits}}.
      If no digits are shown there, no number is on file: ask which mobile number to call.
      The caller may hold for the next free person: {{can_hold}} (true means the team is
      working and everyone is on another call; anything else means holding is not possible).
      One question at a time.
      - They accept: store callback_decision = accepted, but only once there is a number to
        call. When none is on file, get the number first.
      - They name a time: store it in callback_preferred_time as a date and time in UAE time
        with the +04:00 offset, for example 2026-10-08T16:30:00+04:00. Today in the UAE is
        {{local_weekday}} {{local_date}} and the time is {{local_time}}. If no date is shown
        there, do not work out a date yourself: leave callback_preferred_time unset and add
        the time they asked for, in their own words, to the end of handover_summary. Never
        suggest a time yourself. If they ask when we call back, say callbacks are normally
        made {{locale.policy_callback_window}}. If they ask for a time later than that, accept
        it and set callback_later_requested to true. If they ask for a time earlier than that,
        offer the start of that window instead.
      - They want another number, or there is no number: ask for the mobile number, read the
        whole number back in groups of three or four digits and wait for a yes. Then store it
        in reach_number in international format, a plus sign and the country code first, for
        example +971501234567.
      - They do not want a callback: store callback_decision = declined.
      - Only when holding is possible: if they would rather hold for the next free person,
        store callback_decision = wait.
      - No clear answer after you have asked twice: store wait when holding is possible,
        otherwise declined.
      When you store the decision, or a changed request, end your turn with no text at all:
      the next step speaks, and anything you say with it would be heard after that step's
      line. The next step arranges the callback and gives the time: never promise a time and
      never arrange anything yourself.
      If they now ask for a manager, to raise a complaint, about an earlier request or a missed
      call, or for us to stop calling, store that in request_type (manager_requested, complaint,
      chase, missed_call, stop_calling, data_question) and set request_changed to true. If
      they asked to be called back and would now rather speak to someone straight away, store
      request_type = caller_asked and set request_changed to true.
      A safety problem with the car: hand it back at once with __return_to_parent__ and a
      note of what it is about. Without that tool, store request_type = safety_emergency and
      set request_changed to true when the car is not safe to drive, the caller is unsure or
      afraid, or it is a breakdown, an accident, an injury or someone locked in; for anything
      milder put the concern at the start of handover_summary and carry on.
      A request that is none of these: hand it back with __return_to_parent__ and a note of
      what it is about. Without that tool, say one of our team will help with that too,
      rewrite handover_summary so that it starts with the new point and keeps the rest, and
      carry on.
      Summary so far, for you only, never read out: {{handover_summary}}
    AVAILABLE_TOOLS: [get_local_date_time]
    EXIT_WHEN: callback_decision != "pending" OR request_changed == true OR (handover_reason IS SET AND handover_reason != "" AND handover_reason != entry_reason) OR entry_person == true OR entry_complaint == true OR entry_chase == true OR entry_stop_calling == true OR entry_identity_failed == true
    MAX_TURNS: 3
    MAX_ATTEMPTS: 5
    ON_EXHAUSTED: callback_failed
    THEN: after_callback_offer

  # A03: asked for a manager: a manager callback, not a transfer to another contact centre agent.
  manager_callback_start:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      callback_type = "manager_callback"
    THEN: callback_clock

  # A03, with the callback window of Q01.
  # Limit: five turns without an answer, then the callback is treated as not arranged.
  offer_manager_callback:
    REASONING: true
    GOAL: |
      The caller asked for a manager. A manager calls the caller back: a call is never
      transferred to a manager, and a manager request is never passed to another contact
      centre agent. Tell the caller a manager will call them back and ask whether you may
      arrange it on the number ending {{reach_last_digits}} (if no digits are shown there, no
      number is on file: ask which mobile number to call). One question at a time.
      If it is not yet clear what the manager should call about, ask that first in one short
      question, then rewrite handover_summary so that it includes the answer and keeps the rest.
      - They accept: store callback_decision = accepted, but only once there is a number to
        call. When none is on file, get the number first.
      - They name a time: store it in callback_preferred_time as a date and time in UAE time
        with the +04:00 offset, for example 2026-10-08T16:30:00+04:00. Today in the UAE is
        {{local_weekday}} {{local_date}} and the time is {{local_time}}. If no date is shown
        there, do not work out a date yourself: leave callback_preferred_time unset and add
        the time they asked for, in their own words, to the end of handover_summary. Never
        suggest a time yourself. If they ask when the call comes, say callbacks are normally
        made {{locale.policy_callback_window}}. If they ask for a time later than that, accept
        it and set callback_later_requested to true. If they ask for a time earlier than that,
        offer the start of that window instead.
      - They want another number, or there is no number: ask for the mobile number, read the
        whole number back in groups of three or four digits and wait for a yes. Then store it
        in reach_number in international format, a plus sign and the country code first, for
        example +971501234567.
      - They do not want a callback, or give no clear answer after you have asked twice:
        store callback_decision = declined.
      When you store the decision, or a changed request, end your turn with no text at all:
      the next step speaks, and anything you say with it would be heard after that step's
      line. The next step arranges the callback and gives the time: never promise a time and
      never arrange anything yourself.
      If they would now rather speak to one of our team, raise a complaint, ask about an
      earlier request or a missed call, or have us stop calling, store that in request_type
      (caller_asked, complaint, chase, missed_call, stop_calling, data_question) and set
      request_changed to true.
      A safety problem with the car: hand it back at once with __return_to_parent__ and a
      note of what it is about. Without that tool, store request_type = safety_emergency and
      set request_changed to true when the car is not safe to drive, the caller is unsure or
      afraid, or it is a breakdown, an accident, an injury or someone locked in; for anything
      milder put the concern at the start of handover_summary and carry on.
      A request that is none of these: hand it back with __return_to_parent__ and a note of
      what it is about. Without that tool, say one of our team will help with that too,
      rewrite handover_summary so that it starts with the new point and keeps the rest, and
      carry on.
      Summary so far, for you only, never read out: {{handover_summary}}
    AVAILABLE_TOOLS: [get_local_date_time]
    EXIT_WHEN: callback_decision != "pending" OR request_changed == true OR (handover_reason IS SET AND handover_reason != "" AND handover_reason != entry_reason) OR entry_person == true OR entry_complaint == true OR entry_chase == true OR entry_stop_calling == true OR entry_identity_failed == true
    MAX_TURNS: 3
    MAX_ATTEMPTS: 5
    ON_EXHAUSTED: callback_failed
    THEN: after_callback_offer

  after_callback_offer:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: request_changed == true OR (handover_reason IS SET AND handover_reason != "" AND handover_reason != entry_reason) OR entry_person == true OR entry_complaint == true OR entry_chase == true OR entry_stop_calling == true OR entry_identity_failed == true
    ON_FAIL: callback_decision_gate
    THEN: reentry_gate

  callback_decision_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: callback_decision == "accepted"
    ON_FAIL: callback_wait_gate
    THEN: callback_number_gate

  # E27: a caller who would rather hold is put into the queue. Only for a queue callback and
  # only when the queue was found open on this visit; a manager request never takes this road
  # (A03), and neither does a caller who asked to be called back.
  callback_wait_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: callback_decision == "wait" AND callback_type == "queue_callback" AND can_hold == true
    ON_FAIL: callback_declined
    THEN: connect_person

  # The caller does not want a callback. They stay on the line, so the closing question follows.
  callback_declined:
    REASONING: false
    RESPOND: "No problem."
    MESSAGE_KEY: no_problem
    THEN: ask_anything_else

  # The number must be a real number in international format. The language of the callback is
  # English or Arabic, the two the scheduling tool takes: Arabic when the call is in Arabic,
  # otherwise English. Q03: the summary that goes with the callback also carries the booking
  # reference that came with the escape.
  callback_number_gate:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      reach_last_digits = COALESCE(REGEX_EXTRACT(reach_number, "[0-9]{3}$"), "")
      callback_language = COALESCE(REGEX_EXTRACT(language, "^(ar|en)"), "en")
      callback_summary = TRIM(REPLACE(REPLACE("__SUMMARY__ __NOTE__", "__SUMMARY__", handover_summary), "__NOTE__", COALESCE(reference_note, "")))
    CHECK: reach_number.matches("^[+][0-9]{8,15}$")
    ON_FAIL: callback_failed
    THEN: callback_later_gate

  # OPEN Q01 (contact centre): Is this still right? "Later only if the customer asks" is the
  # interim rule. Set TOYOTA_HANDOVER_CALLBACK_LATER_ON_REQUEST to "false" to refuse later times.
  callback_later_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: callback_later_requested == true AND ("{{env.TOYOTA_HANDOVER_CALLBACK_LATER_ON_REQUEST}}" == "false")
    ON_FAIL: schedule_callback_step
    THEN: callback_window_only

  callback_window_only:
    REASONING: false
    CLEAR: [callback_preferred_time]
    RESPOND: "We make callbacks during our working hours, so I'll book the next available time for you."
    MESSAGE_KEY: callback_window_only
    THEN: schedule_callback_step

  # E29 (queue_callback) and A03 (manager_callback), the only two callback types this agent
  # uses. The summary goes with the callback so the person who calls back does not ask again
  # (Q03). The preferred time, when the caller gave one, is ISO 8601 with +04:00; the backend
  # enforces the callback window (Q01). The contact name is the caller's own name, or the
  # profile name once the caller has been identified.
  # The number the caller has just accepted or given for the callback is the contact number of
  # this call from here on (session contract: contact_mobile), so a later task on the same call
  # does not ask for it again.
  schedule_callback_step:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      contact_mobile = reach_number
    CALL: schedule_callback
      WITH:
        callback_type: callback_type
        mobile_number: reach_number
        reason: person_reason
