        summary: FIRST_NON_EMPTY(callback_summary, handover_summary)
        preferred_time: callback_preferred_time
        language: callback_language
        customer_name: contact_name
      AS: callback_result
    ON_RESULT:
      - IF: callback_result.scheduled == true
        THEN: confirm_callback
      - ELSE:
        THEN: callback_failed
    ON_FAILURE:
      THEN: callback_failed

  # Every callback ends with one short sentence: who calls, on which number and when. The time
  # is the one the scheduling tool returned (callback_scheduled_for, already UAE time).
  # The sentence is worded in the caller's language by this step and written to spoken_line;
  # the fixed step say_spoken_line says it and the closing question follows it (see "Order of
  # speech" above FLOW). The step always ends after one pass; say_outcome_gate decides what is
  # said.
  confirm_callback:
    REASONING: true
    GOAL: |
      The callback is arranged. Write spoken_line: one short sentence, in the language the
      caller is speaking (English or Gulf Arabic) and worded exactly as it is to be said on
      the phone, that tells the caller who will call (callback type {{callback_type}}:
      queue_callback means one of our team, manager_callback means a manager), on the number
      ending {{reach_last_digits}}, and when: {{callback_scheduled_for}}.
      That time is already UAE time: word the day and the time the way people say them. Today
      in the UAE is {{local_weekday}} {{local_date}}.
      If no time is shown, write only that the callback is arranged and name no time. If no
      digits are shown for the number, do not mention the number. Put nothing else into the
      sentence and no question: a later step asks whether they need anything else.
      Save spoken_line with your session context tool and call no other tool. Do not say
      anything yourself in this step: the next step says what you write, and anything you say
      here would be heard a second time, after the closing question. After writing
      spoken_line, end your turn with no text at all.
    AVAILABLE_TOOLS: [get_local_date_time]
    EXIT_WHEN: always
    MAX_TURNS: 2
    THEN: say_outcome_gate

  # The three outcome sentences (callback arranged, complaint raised, chase recorded) are said
  # here, by a fixed step, from what the model wrote. If nothing was written, a short fixed
  # line stands in, so the caller always hears that the task was done before the closing
  # question. All three steps are reached only after the tool reported success.
  say_outcome_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: spoken_line IS SET AND spoken_line != ""
    ON_FAIL: say_outcome_done
    THEN: say_spoken_line

  say_spoken_line:
    REASONING: false
    RESPOND: "{{spoken_line}}"
    MESSAGE_KEY: spoken_line
    THEN: ask_anything_else

  say_outcome_done:
    REASONING: false
    RESPOND: "That's done for you."
    MESSAGE_KEY: outcome_done
    THEN: ask_anything_else

  # The callback could not be arranged, or the caller gave no clear answer. When the queue
  # was found open on this visit a queue callback falls back to holding for a person;
  # otherwise say it plainly.
  callback_failed:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: callback_type == "queue_callback" AND can_hold == true
    ON_FAIL: callback_not_arranged
    THEN: connect_person

  # Nobody can be reached now and no callback could be arranged. The caller stays on the line,
  # so the closing question follows.
  callback_not_arranged:
    REASONING: false
    RESPOND: "I'm sorry, I couldn't arrange the callback just now, so please call us again."
    MESSAGE_KEY: callback_not_arranged
    THEN: ask_anything_else

  # ---- Complaints -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # OPEN N21 (contact centre): How often does the contact centre get this call?
  # Interim: take the details and raise the ticket. Set TOYOTA_HANDOVER_COMPLAINT_MODE to
  # "transfer" to pass complaints to a person instead (the alternative the document states).
  # The ready flag is put back to false here so that it can only come from the step that takes
  # the details and confirms the number for the ticket message.
  complaint_mode_gate:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      complaint_ready = false
    CHECK: ("{{env.TOYOTA_HANDOVER_COMPLAINT_MODE}}" == "transfer")
    ON_FAIL: complaint_demo_gate
    THEN: complaint_transfer_ack

  # Demo overlay (journey 09, E120): the step that takes a complaint asks for the caller's own
  # name and confirms or takes a mobile number, and a ticket message then goes to that number.
  # No attendee is asked for real details at the Summit, so in the demonstration a complaint
  # is acknowledged and takes the road to a person, where the advisor line is said (E123) and
  # the demonstration carries on. Assumption: the document does not say what a complaint does
  # at the Summit; this is the choice that asks nothing and raises nothing.
  complaint_demo_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: ("{{env.TOYOTA_DEMO_MODE}}" == "true")
    ON_FAIL: take_complaint
    THEN: complaint_transfer_ack

  # E28 when complaints are passed to a person: acknowledged first, with the fixed line.
  complaint_transfer_ack:
    REASONING: false
    RESPOND: "I'm sorry about the trouble you've had."
    MESSAGE_KEY: upset_acknowledgement
    THEN: complaint_to_person

  # N21: takes the details. E28: acknowledges first.
  # The complaint is in the caller's own name. A name is asked for only when none is known:
  # the caller's own name, or the profile name once the caller has been identified.
  # Limit: six turns without the details and a confirmed number, then a person takes over.
  take_complaint:
    REASONING: true
    GOAL: |
      The caller wants to raise a complaint. You take the details; the next step raises it
      with the complaints team.
      If it has not been done yet on this call, acknowledge how they feel and apologise once.
      Then find out, one question at a time and only what you do not already know from this
      call: what happened, when, and which service centre or showroom it was.
      Store complaint_details: the complaint in the caller's own words, in plain English, with
      the date and the centre or showroom. Store complaint_category: one of service_quality,
      repeat_problem, billing, delay, staff_conduct, sales, delivery, unanswered_request, other.
      Caller's name: {{contact_name}}. If no name is shown there, ask for their name once and
      store it in caller_name. Never say a name from our records to the caller.
      Then tell the caller the ticket number will come by text message to the number ending
      {{reach_last_digits}} and check that it is the right number (if no digits are shown
      there, no number is on file: ask for the mobile number). If they give another number,
      read the whole number back in groups of three or four digits and wait for a yes. Then
      store it in reach_number in international format, a plus sign and the country code
      first, for example +971501234567.
      When the details are taken and the number is confirmed, set complaint_ready to true and
      end your turn with no text at all: the next steps raise the complaint and speak, and
      anything you say with it would be heard after their lines.
      Never say who was at fault, never promise an outcome, a refund, a discount or
      compensation, and never say when the reply will come: the next step does that.
      If they would rather speak to one of our team or a manager or be called back, or now
      ask about an earlier request, a missed call or for us to stop calling, store that in
      request_type (caller_asked, callback_requested, manager_requested, chase, missed_call,
      stop_calling, data_question) and set request_changed to true. If they no longer want to
      raise the complaint, store request_type = withdrawn and set request_changed to true.
      Whenever you set request_changed, say nothing more: the next step speaks.
      A safety problem with the car: hand it back at once with __return_to_parent__ and a
      note of what it is about. Without that tool, store request_type = safety_emergency and
      set request_changed to true when the car is not safe to drive, the caller is unsure or
      afraid, or it is a breakdown, an accident, an injury or someone locked in; for anything
      milder add the concern to complaint_details and carry on.
      A request that is none of these: hand it back with __return_to_parent__ and a note of
      what it is about. Without that tool, say one of our team will help with that too and
      carry on.
    AVAILABLE_TOOLS: [get_local_date_time]
    EXIT_WHEN: complaint_ready == true OR request_changed == true OR (handover_reason IS SET AND handover_reason != "" AND handover_reason != entry_reason) OR entry_person == true OR entry_complaint == true OR entry_chase == true OR entry_stop_calling == true OR entry_identity_failed == true
    MAX_TURNS: 3
    MAX_ATTEMPTS: 6
    ON_EXHAUSTED: complaint_to_person
    VOICE:
      END_OF_SPEECH_TURN_TYPE: complex_explanation
    THEN: after_complaint

  after_complaint:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: request_changed == true OR (handover_reason IS SET AND handover_reason != "" AND handover_reason != entry_reason) OR entry_person == true OR entry_complaint == true OR entry_chase == true OR entry_stop_calling == true OR entry_identity_failed == true
    ON_FAIL: complaint_ready_gate
    THEN: reentry_gate

  # The number for the ticket message must be a real number in international format. The name
  # the caller has just given, when one was asked for, becomes the contact name.
  complaint_ready_gate:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      reach_last_digits = COALESCE(REGEX_EXTRACT(reach_number, "[0-9]{3}$"), "")
      contact_name = COALESCE(FIRST_NON_EMPTY(caller_name, contact_name, ""), "")
      callback_language = COALESCE(REGEX_EXTRACT(language, "^(ar|en)"), "en")
    CHECK: complaint_ready == true AND complaint_details != "" AND reach_number.matches("^[+][0-9]{8,15}$")
    ON_FAIL: complaint_to_person
    THEN: raise_complaint

  # N21: raises the complaint, as the contact centre does today. A ticket that comes back
  # without a number is still raised: nothing is texted and the caller is told so.
  # The number the caller has just confirmed or given for the ticket message is the contact
  # number of this call from here on (session contract: contact_mobile).
  raise_complaint:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      contact_mobile = reach_number
    CALL: create_complaint
      WITH:
        mobile_number: reach_number
        category: complaint_category
        details: complaint_details
        customer_name: contact_name
        plate_number: plate_number
      AS: complaint_result
    ON_RESULT:
      - IF: complaint_result.created == true AND complaint_result.ticket_number != ""
        SET:
          complaint_response_time = complaint_result.response_time
        THEN: send_ticket_message
      - IF: complaint_result.created == true
        SET:
          complaint_response_time = complaint_result.response_time
        THEN: confirm_complaint
      - ELSE:
        THEN: complaint_failed
    ON_FAILURE:
      THEN: complaint_failed

  # N21: ticket number by SMS. This agent sends it: the complaints system sends no message for
  # a ticket the AI agent raises. The channel is SMS, as the case says, so no WhatsApp retry is
  # needed. The read-out in the next step is the backup when the message could not be sent.
  send_ticket_message:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      ticket_message_sent = false
    CALL: send_customer_message
      WITH:
        mobile_number: reach_number
        template: "complaint_ticket"
        channel: "sms"
        reference: complaint_ticket_number
        reference_type: "complaint"
        language: callback_language
      AS: ticket_message
    ON_RESULT:
      - IF: ticket_message.sent == true
        SET:
          ticket_message_sent = true
        THEN: confirm_complaint
      - ELSE:
        THEN: confirm_complaint
    ON_FAILURE:
      THEN: confirm_complaint

  # N21: the complaints team calls within 2 working days (interim, open). The time the tool
  # returns wins; the locale key policy_complaint_response is the fallback wording.
  # The ticket number is read out only when the text message could not be sent; when it was
  # sent, the caller hears where it is going. The sentences are worded in the caller's
  # language by this step and written to spoken_line; say_spoken_line says them and the
  # closing question follows in its own step.
  confirm_complaint:
    REASONING: true
    GOAL: |
      The complaint has been raised. Write spoken_line: two short sentences at most, in the
      language the caller is speaking (English or Gulf Arabic) and worded exactly as they are
      to be said on the phone, that tell the caller:
      - that the complaint is raised;
      - text message sent: {{ticket_message_sent}}. If true, that the ticket number is on its
        way by text message to the number ending {{reach_last_digits}}, without the ticket
        number itself. If it is not true, that the text message could not be sent, then the
        ticket number {{complaint_ticket_number}} written one character at a time with a
        space between the characters so that it is read out that way, and ask them to note
        it. If no ticket number is shown there, never make one up: write that the complaints
        team will give them the number;
      - when the complaints team will call: {{complaint_response_time}}. If that is empty, use
        {{locale.policy_complaint_response}}.
      Promise nothing else and put no other question into it: a later step asks whether they
      need anything else.
      Save spoken_line with your session context tool and call no other tool. Do not say
      anything yourself in this step: the next step says what you write, and anything you say
      here would be heard a second time, after the closing question. After writing
      spoken_line, end your turn with no text at all.
    AVAILABLE_TOOLS: [get_local_date_time]
    EXIT_WHEN: always
    MAX_TURNS: 2
    THEN: say_outcome_gate

  # N21 "or passes the call to a person": the flag, a caller who cannot give the details, or a
  # number that cannot be confirmed. The call goes to the complaints queue.
  complaint_to_person:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      person_reason = "complaint"
      route_queue = "complaints"
    CLEAR: [handover_summary]
    THEN: person_gate

  complaint_failed:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      person_reason = "complaint_not_raised"
      route_queue = "complaints"
    CLEAR: [handover_summary]
    RESPOND: "I'm sorry, I couldn't raise your complaint just now."
    MESSAGE_KEY: complaint_not_raised
    THEN: person_gate

  # ---- Stop calling me --------------------------------------------------------------------
  # OPEN N25 (contact centre): How often does the contact centre get this call?
  # Interim: record do not call and confirm it. Set TOYOTA_HANDOVER_DNC_RECORD to "false" to
  # pass these callers to a person instead.
  dnc_mode_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: ("{{env.TOYOTA_HANDOVER_DNC_RECORD}}" == "false")
    ON_FAIL: number_gate
    THEN: dnc_to_person

  # OPEN N23 (contact centre): How often does the contact centre get this call?
  # Interim: look up why we called. Set TOYOTA_HANDOVER_MISSED_CALL_RETURN to "false" to skip
  # the look-up and simply ask how we can help.
  missed_call_mode_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: request_type == "missed_call" AND ("{{env.TOYOTA_HANDOVER_MISSED_CALL_RETURN}}" == "false")
    ON_FAIL: number_gate
    THEN: ask_how_to_help

  # The look-up and the do-not-call record always use the caller's own line: the number they are
  # calling from, then the contact number on file. A number given earlier in this visit for a
  # callback or a message is never used here. Only a real phone number counts (a withheld
  # caller id is not one).
  number_gate:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      reach_number = COALESCE(FIRST_NON_EMPTY(REGEX_EXTRACT(caller_phone, "^[+][0-9]{8,15}$"), REGEX_EXTRACT(contact_mobile, "^[+][0-9]{8,15}$")), "")
      reach_last_digits = COALESCE(REGEX_EXTRACT(FIRST_NON_EMPTY(REGEX_EXTRACT(caller_phone, "^[+][0-9]{8,15}$"), REGEX_EXTRACT(contact_mobile, "^[+][0-9]{8,15}$")), "[0-9]{3}$"), "")
    CHECK: reach_number.matches("^[+][0-9]{8,15}$")
    ON_FAIL: number_missing_gate
    THEN: contact_task_gate

  # N23: with no usable number nothing can be found, so a returned missed call is asked how we
  # can help. A stop-calling request or a chase without a number goes to a person.
  number_missing_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: request_type == "missed_call"
    ON_FAIL: number_missing
    THEN: ask_how_to_help

  contact_task_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: request_type == "stop_calling"
    ON_FAIL: lookup_requests
    THEN: record_dnc

  # N25: records do not call.
  record_dnc:
    REASONING: false
    CALL: record_do_not_call
      WITH:
        mobile_number: reach_number
        requested_by: "customer_on_call"
      AS: dnc_result
    ON_RESULT:
      - IF: dnc_result.recorded == true
        THEN: confirm_dnc
      - ELSE:
        THEN: tool_failed
    ON_FAILURE:
      THEN: tool_failed

  # N25: confirms it.
  confirm_dnc:
    REASONING: false
    RESPOND: "I've recorded that you don't want us to call you."
    MESSAGE_KEY: dnc_confirmed
    THEN: dnc_followup_gate

  # N25: questions about their data go to a person. With no such question the caller stays on
  # the line, so the closing question follows.
  dnc_followup_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: wants_data_answer == true
    ON_FAIL: ask_anything_else
    THEN: data_to_person

  dnc_to_person:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      person_reason = "stop_calling_request"
    CLEAR: [handover_summary]
    THEN: person_gate

  data_to_person:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      person_reason = "data_question"
    CLEAR: [handover_summary]
    THEN: person_gate

  number_missing:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      person_reason = "no_contact_number"
    CLEAR: [handover_summary]
    THEN: person_gate

  # ---- Chases and returned missed calls ---------------------------------------------------
  # A02: the chase steps start at once: what is open on the caller's number.
  # N23: the same look-up says why we last called, as a code (last_outbound_call.reason_code:
  # lead, booking_reminder, callback, survey or other; empty when we did not call). Each of the
  # three reasons the case names has its own fixed, localised line; any other reason is put
  # into words from the tool's text; no reason at all means nothing was found.
  # Every branch names the result it needs, so none of them matches after a failed look-up.
  lookup_requests:
    REASONING: false
    CALL: get_open_requests
      WITH:
        mobile_number: reach_number
      AS: open_requests
    ON_RESULT:
      - IF: request_type == "missed_call" AND open_requests.last_outbound_call.reason_code == "lead"
        THEN: missed_call_lead
      - IF: request_type == "missed_call" AND open_requests.last_outbound_call.reason_code == "booking_reminder"
        THEN: missed_call_reminder
      - IF: request_type == "missed_call" AND open_requests.last_outbound_call.reason_code == "callback"
        THEN: missed_call_callback
      - IF: request_type == "missed_call" AND open_requests.total >= 0 AND open_requests.last_outbound_call_reason != ""
        SET:
          missed_call_reason = open_requests.last_outbound_call_reason
        THEN: explain_missed_call
      - IF: request_type == "missed_call" AND open_requests.total >= 0
        THEN: ask_how_to_help
      - IF: open_requests.total > 0
        SET:
          open_requests_list = open_requests.requests
        THEN: choose_request
      - ELSE:
        THEN: chase_to_person
    ON_FAILURE:
      THEN: tool_failed

  # A02: which open request the caller is chasing, without asking when it is already clear.
  # When it is clear the step ends with no text: the chase is recorded behind the hold line
  # and the next step says what was done.
  # Limit: the caller is asked at most twice; the third unclear answer goes to a person.
  choose_request:
    REASONING: true
    GOAL: |
      The caller is chasing an earlier request. These requests are open on their number:
      {{#each open_requests_list}}
      - id {{this.request_id}}: {{this.type}} with {{this.team}}, opened {{this.created_date}}: {{this.summary}}
      {{/each}}
      Work out which one the caller means from what they have already said. If only one is
      open and it fits, or it is clear which one they mean, store its id in chase_request_id,
      ask nothing and end your turn with no text at all. If it is not clear, ask one short
      question that names the teams or the topics, never the ids. If none of them is what the
      caller is chasing, store chase_request_id = none and end your turn with no text.
      Read out nothing from the requests beyond the team and the topic, and promise nothing:
      the next step records the chase and says what was done.
      If they now want a person, a call back, a manager, to raise a new complaint or for us to
      stop calling, store that in request_type (caller_asked, callback_requested,
      manager_requested, complaint, stop_calling, data_question) and set request_changed to
      true. If they no longer want to follow it up, store request_type = withdrawn and set
      request_changed to true. Whenever you set request_changed, say nothing more: the next
      step speaks.
      A safety problem with the car: hand it back at once with __return_to_parent__ and a
      note of what it is about. Without that tool, store request_type = safety_emergency and
      set request_changed to true when the car is not safe to drive, the caller is unsure or
      afraid, or it is a breakdown, an accident, an injury or someone locked in.
      A request that is none of these: hand it back with __return_to_parent__ and a note of
      what it is about. Without that tool, say one of our team will help with that too and
      carry on.
    AVAILABLE_TOOLS: [get_local_date_time]
    EXIT_WHEN: chase_request_id != "pending" OR request_changed == true OR (handover_reason IS SET AND handover_reason != "" AND handover_reason != entry_reason) OR entry_person == true OR entry_complaint == true OR entry_chase == true OR entry_stop_calling == true OR entry_identity_failed == true
    MAX_TURNS: 3
    MAX_ATTEMPTS: 3
    ON_EXHAUSTED: chase_to_person
    VOICE:
      END_OF_SPEECH_TURN_TYPE: open_ended_question
    THEN: after_choose_request

  after_choose_request:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: request_changed == true OR (handover_reason IS SET AND handover_reason != "" AND handover_reason != entry_reason) OR entry_person == true OR entry_complaint == true OR entry_chase == true OR entry_stop_calling == true OR entry_identity_failed == true
    ON_FAIL: chase_match_gate
    THEN: reentry_gate

  chase_match_gate:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: chase_request_id != "pending" AND chase_request_id != "none" AND chase_request_id != ""
    ON_FAIL: chase_to_person
    THEN: record_chase_step

  # OPEN Q04 (Aftersales workshop): Should the second call go to a person instead of a follow-up email?
  # Interim: the contact centre rule behind record_chase sends a follow-up email on the second
  # call and raises a complaint on the third; the caller is told what it did. Set
  # TOYOTA_HANDOVER_CHASE_SECOND_CALL to "person" to pass the second call to a person. The
  # second call is the one on which the rule answers with the action code followup_email. The
  # chase is still recorded first so that the count stays right, which means the rule behind
  # record_chase has already acted (today: the follow-up email). Sending no email on that call
  # is a change to that rule, not to this agent; the person is told what was done in the summary.
  record_chase_step:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      chase_note = FIRST_NON_EMPTY(caller_statement, "The caller phoned to chase this request.")
    CALL: record_chase
      WITH:
        request_id: chase_request_id
        summary: chase_note
      AS: chase_result
    ON_RESULT:
      - IF: ("{{env.TOYOTA_HANDOVER_CHASE_SECOND_CALL}}" == "person") AND chase_result.action_code == "followup_email"
        SET:
          chase_action_taken = chase_result.action_taken
        THEN: second_chase_to_person
      - IF: chase_result.action_code == "complaint"
        SET:
          chase_action_taken = chase_result.action_taken
          chase_ticket_number = chase_result.ticket_number
          chase_expected_response = chase_result.expected_response
        THEN: tell_chase_outcome
      - ELSE:
        SET:
          chase_action_taken = chase_result.action_taken
        THEN: tell_chase_outcome
    ON_FAILURE:
      THEN: tool_failed

  # Q04: says what the rule did (follow-up email on the second call, complaint on the third).
  # The branch above goes by the action code the tool returns, not by the count. When the rule
  # raised a complaint, the caller hears its ticket number and when the complaints team calls,
  # both from the tool.
  # The sentences are worded in the caller's language by this step and written to
  # spoken_line; say_spoken_line says them and the closing question follows in its own step.
  tell_chase_outcome:
    REASONING: true
    GOAL: |
      The caller's chase has been recorded. What the contact centre rule did:
      {{chase_action_taken}}
      Write spoken_line: one or two short sentences, in the language the caller is speaking
      (English or Gulf Arabic) and worded exactly as they are to be said on the phone, that
      tell the caller that in plain words, with what happens next.
      {{#if chase_ticket_number}}A complaint has been raised for them. Include the ticket number {{chase_ticket_number}}, written one character at a time with a space between the characters so that it is read out that way, and when the complaints team will call: {{chase_expected_response}}. If no time is shown there, use {{locale.policy_complaint_response}}.{{/if}}
      If nothing is stated above, write only that you have recorded that they called about it
      again. Promise nothing that is not stated above and put no question into it: a later
      step asks whether they need anything else.
      Save spoken_line with your session context tool and call no other tool. Do not say
      anything yourself in this step: the next step says what you write, and anything you say
      here would be heard a second time, after the closing question. After writing
      spoken_line, end your turn with no text at all.
    AVAILABLE_TOOLS: [get_local_date_time]
    EXIT_WHEN: always
    MAX_TURNS: 2
    THEN: say_outcome_gate

  # Nothing open on this number, or none of it is what the caller is chasing: a person looks into it.
  chase_to_person:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      person_reason = "chase_request_not_found"
    CLEAR: [handover_summary]
    THEN: person_gate

  second_chase_to_person:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      person_reason = "second_chase"
    CLEAR: [handover_summary]
    THEN: person_gate

  # N23: why we called, and the caller picks it up from there. Each line gives only the general
  # reason (no name, plate, date or other record detail: the specialist confirms who is calling
  # first) and ends in a question, so nothing is added after it. The step completes, the
  # supervisor waits, and it routes the caller's answer to the specialist who picks it up:
  # sales for a lead, booking changes for a reminder, whatever they then ask for after a callback.
  # We called about a sales enquiry (a lead).
  missed_call_lead:
    REASONING: false
    RESPOND: "We called about your enquiry about a Toyota. How can I help you with it?"
    MESSAGE_KEY: missed_call_lead
    THEN: finish

  # We called to remind them of a service booking (a reminder).
  missed_call_reminder:
    REASONING: false
    RESPOND: "We called to remind you about your service booking. Would you like to confirm it or change it?"
    MESSAGE_KEY: missed_call_reminder
    THEN: finish

  # We called because they had asked for a call back (a callback).
  missed_call_callback:
    REASONING: false
    RESPOND: "We called because you asked us to call you back. How can I help you?"
    MESSAGE_KEY: missed_call_callback
    THEN: finish

  # N23: we called for another reason (a survey, or one the tool gives only in words). The
  # general reason is put into the caller's language, with the same closing question.
  explain_missed_call:
    REASONING: true
    CONTEXT_UPDATES: false
    GOAL: |
      The caller is returning a missed call from us. Why we called: {{missed_call_reason}}
      Tell them the general reason in one short sentence, then ask how you can help. Read out
      no names, plate numbers, dates, prices or other record details. Say nothing else and use
      no tool: the right specialist picks up their answer.
    AVAILABLE_TOOLS: [get_local_date_time]
    EXIT_WHEN: always
    MAX_TURNS: 2
    THEN: finish

  # N23: nothing found: asks how it can help. The supervisor routes the answer. The same line
  # is used when the look-up is switched off or there is no number to look up, so it does not
  # claim that a search was made.
  ask_how_to_help:
    REASONING: false
    RESPOND: "I don't have a note of why we called you. How can I help you today?"
    MESSAGE_KEY: missed_call_not_found
    THEN: finish

  # ---- Failures ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # A tool did not answer after its one retry, a model call failed (ON_ERROR) or a constraint
  # stopped a tool: say so briefly (the shared line, which promises nothing), then a person
  # helps. A second failure in the same visit takes the short road below, which makes no model
  # call and no tool call, so it cannot loop. The trouble line is said once in a visit: the
  # second failure goes to the connecting line without it.
  # A failure that arrives after the live hand-over was started (connect_person) can only be
  # the hand-over itself. Every road below ends in connect_person again, so without this first
  # check a transfer that cannot be made would be tried again and again, the connecting line
  # said each time. It is tried once: the caller is told, and the flow ends on the closing
  # question (transfer_not_made), as the safety agent and the front desk do in the same case.
  tool_failed:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: transfer_started == true
    ON_FAIL: count_failure
    THEN: transfer_not_made

  count_failure:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      failure_count = ADD(failure_count, 1)
      person_reason = FIRST_NON_EMPTY(handover_reason, "system_error")
    CHECK: failure_count < 2
    ON_FAIL: hard_failure
    THEN: tool_trouble_line

  # The live hand-over could not be made. The caller stays on the line, so the closing
  # question follows; a caller who asks for a person again is routed here afresh.
  transfer_not_made:
    REASONING: false
    RESPOND: "I'm sorry, I couldn't connect you just now."
    MESSAGE_KEY: could_not_connect
    THEN: ask_anything_else

  tool_trouble_line:
    REASONING: false
    RESPOND: "I'm sorry, I'm having trouble with that just now."
    MESSAGE_KEY: system_trouble
    THEN: person_gate

  # Straight to a person with whatever summary there is. The demo gate applies here too
  # (E122, E123).
  hard_failure:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      handover_summary = FIRST_NON_EMPTY(handover_summary, entry_summary, caller_statement, "The assistant had a technical problem before a summary was captured. Please ask the caller how you can help.")
      person_reason = FIRST_NON_EMPTY(person_reason, handover_reason, request_type)
    CHECK: ("{{env.TOYOTA_DEMO_MODE}}" == "true")
    ON_FAIL: hard_failure_route
    THEN: demo_gate

  # A03 holds even here: a manager request is never transferred to a contact centre agent.
  hard_failure_route:
    REASONING: false
    CHECK: request_type.contains("manager") OR request_type.contains("supervisor") OR person_reason.matches("^manager")
    ON_FAIL: connect_person
    THEN: callback_not_arranged

  # ---- Leaving without a transfer ---------------------------------------------------------
  # The supervisor adds nothing after this agent returns. Every path that finishes a task and
  # leaves the caller on the line (callback arranged, declined or not arranged, complaint
  # raised, chase recorded, do not call recorded, and the advisor line of the demonstration)
  # therefore ends here, with the shared line in the caller's language. Paths whose last line
  # is already a question (a returned missed call) and the demo close line, which ends the
  # call, go straight to finish. Like finish, the step drops the copies of the hand-over
  # fields before it completes. spoken_line is not touched here: it has just been said, and
  # start empties it at the next visit.
  ask_anything_else:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      route_queue = "toyota_service"
      reentry_count = 0
    CLEAR: [handover_reason, handover_summary, handover_queue, booking_reference, entry_summary, open_requests_list, callback_preferred_time]
    RESPOND: "Is there anything else I can help you with?"
    MESSAGE_KEY: anything_else
    THEN: COMPLETE

  # The task is done without a transfer and the last line said needs no closing question. The
  # copies of the hand-over fields are dropped so a later visit in the same call starts clean.
  # end_call is left as it is.
  finish:
    REASONING: false
    SET:
      route_queue = "toyota_service"
      reentry_count = 0
    CLEAR: [handover_reason, handover_summary, handover_queue, booking_reference, entry_summary, open_requests_list, callback_preferred_time]
    THEN: COMPLETE

# E27, E28, Q03: the live hand-over. Transfer method and SIP target are project settings
# (Agent Transfer); nothing here names a number or an address.
# OPEN Q03 (contact centre): What else does the contact centre need to see?
# Interim list below: the summary first, then the reason code and the queue, who is calling
# (both names, both numbers, and whether the caller was identified), the car, and the booking
# reference that came with the escape.
# Routing: the call goes to the queue that was checked (route_queue). The list is read from the
# top and the first entry whose condition holds is used; the last entry is the general queue
# for a name that is none of the others. The roadside entry is the urgent road.
ESCALATE:
  context_for_human:
    - handover_summary
    - handover_reason
    - route_queue
    - caller_phone
    - contact_mobile
    - caller_name
    - customer_name
    - identity_status
    - crm_customer_id
    - plate_number
    - vehicle_model
    - booking_reference
    - conversation_history

  routing:
    - id: roadside_queue
      WHEN: route_queue == "roadside"
      queue: "roadside"
      voice:
        call_transfer_type: sip
        transfer_method: refer
      metadata:
        handover_reason: "{{handover_reason}}"
        skill_queue: "{{route_queue}}"
        urgency: "urgent"
        caller_phone: "{{caller_phone}}"
        plate_number: "{{plate_number}}"
        booking_reference: "{{booking_reference}}"

    - id: sales_queue
      WHEN: route_queue == "toyota_sales"
      queue: "toyota_sales"
      voice:
        call_transfer_type: sip
        transfer_method: refer
      metadata:
        handover_reason: "{{handover_reason}}"
        skill_queue: "{{route_queue}}"
        caller_phone: "{{caller_phone}}"
        plate_number: "{{plate_number}}"
        booking_reference: "{{booking_reference}}"

    - id: complaints_queue
      WHEN: route_queue == "complaints"
      queue: "complaints"
      voice:
        call_transfer_type: sip
        transfer_method: refer
      metadata:
        handover_reason: "{{handover_reason}}"
        skill_queue: "{{route_queue}}"
        caller_phone: "{{caller_phone}}"
        plate_number: "{{plate_number}}"
        booking_reference: "{{booking_reference}}"

    - id: service_queue
      WHEN: route_queue == "toyota_service"
      queue: "toyota_service"
      voice:
        call_transfer_type: sip
        transfer_method: refer
      metadata:
        handover_reason: "{{handover_reason}}"
        skill_queue: "{{route_queue}}"
        caller_phone: "{{caller_phone}}"
        plate_number: "{{plate_number}}"
        booking_reference: "{{booking_reference}}"

    - id: general_queue
      WHEN: always
      queue: "toyota_contact_centre"
      voice:
        call_transfer_type: sip
        transfer_method: refer
      metadata:
        handover_reason: "{{handover_reason}}"
        skill_queue: "{{route_queue}}"
        caller_phone: "{{caller_phone}}"
        plate_number: "{{plate_number}}"
        booking_reference: "{{booking_reference}}"

# A failed tool call is handled by the step's own ON_FAILURE (the tool library already retries
# once). Every other failure goes to the tool_failed step, which counts failures and takes the
# short, demo-aware road on the second one. No handler speaks: the steps do, in the caller's language.
ON_ERROR:
  tool_error:
    RETRY: 0
    THEN: CONTINUE

  llm_error:
    RETRY: 1
    THEN: BACKTRACK
    BACKTRACK_TO: tool_failed

  validation_error:
    RETRY: 0
    THEN: BACKTRACK
    BACKTRACK_TO: tool_failed

  routing_error:
    RETRY: 0
    THEN: BACKTRACK
    BACKTRACK_TO: tool_failed

  timeout_error:
    RETRY: 0
    THEN: BACKTRACK
    BACKTRACK_TO: tool_failed

  unknown_error:
    RETRY: 0
    THEN: BACKTRACK
    BACKTRACK_TO: tool_failed
